fields.ic_name: ARM Serial Wire Debug (SWD) — ADIv5 (ARM IHI 0031C)
fields.dft_architecture_summary: ADIv5 SWD is fundamentally a DEBUG-access architecture, not a DFT (manufacturing test) architecture in the classical IEEE 1149.1 sense. SWD does not implement boundary-scan cells on every external I/O pin; it does not enable EXTEST/INTEST/RUNBIST as JTAG TAPs do. The 'DFT' that SWD provides is in-system controllability and observability of the CPU + system bus via the MEM-AP: the debug host can halt the CPU, single-step it, read/write its registers, dump memory, configure FPB/DWT hardware breakpoints/watchpoints, and read CoreSight ITM/DWT trace via the SWO pin. For boundary-scan-style manufacturing test of board interconnects, SoCs typically expose a 4-pin JTAG-DP (or the SWJ-DP's JTAG mode) alongside SWD; the SWD-side cannot do EXTEST.

debug_access_architecture_topology.description: Host → SW-DP (wire-level FSM + 46-bit transaction processing) → DP register set → AP bus (up to 256 APs) → MEM-AP (CSW + TAR + DRW) → SoC system bus (AHB/AXI/APB) → all memory-mapped resources including CPU debug-control registers and CoreSight components.
key_components_reached: Cortex-M Debug Control Block (DCB): DHCSR (Debug Halting Control/Status), DCRSR (Debug Core Register Selector), DCRDR (Debug Core Register Data), DEMCR (Debug Exception and Monitor Control).
Flash Patch & Breakpoint Unit (FPB) — hardware breakpoint comparators.
Data Watchpoint & Trace Unit (DWT) — hardware watchpoint comparators + PC sampling + cycle counter.
Instrumentation Trace Macrocell (ITM) — printf-style trace + DWT-event trace → SWO.
Embedded Trace Macrocell (ETM) — full instruction-and-data trace → TPIU → trace pins.
Cross-Trigger Interface (CTI) — debug-event synchronization across cores.
Trace Port Interface Unit (TPIU) — funnels ITM + ETM trace to the SWO or parallel TRACEDATA pins.
CoreSight ROM Tables — enumerate all the above components.

fields.internal_scan_optional: Beyond ADIv5 SWD, SoCs typically implement traditional internal scan chains (full-scan / partial-scan flip-flops) accessed via the SWJ-DP's JTAG mode (4-pin TAP). These are vendor-specific and orthogonal to SWD. ADIv5 itself does not standardize internal scan chains.
fields.bist_optional: RUNBIST is a JTAG instruction (IEEE 1149.1) NOT an SWD feature. SoCs that implement BIST typically initiate it via a vendor-specific MEM-AP-reachable BIST control register OR via the SWJ-DP's JTAG mode with RUNBIST.
applications_documented_in_adiv5: Cortex-M CPU debug — halt, resume, single-step, breakpoints, watchpoints, register access, memory access.
Flash programming via the MEM-AP's system-bus master role.
Multi-core SoC debug coordination via CTI.
ITM / DWT trace capture via SWO.
ETM trace capture via TPIU trace pins.
Boot ROM / secure boot enrolment via vendor-specific MEM-AP registers.
Debug authentication via DBGEN/NIDEN/SPIDEN/SPNIDEN gating (optional, vendor-specific).
Post-production debug-disable via vendor fuse (RDP / APPROTECT / DCFG).
test_methodologies: Debug Access (not classical DFT) — host pretends to be a bus master on the SoC's debug bus.
CoreSight Trace Capture — host receives trace packets on SWO (or TRACEDATA pins) for post-mortem analysis.
BIST initiation via vendor-specific MEM-AP registers — host triggers BIST and reads the result from a known address.
Internal Scan Test — orthogonal to ADIv5; typically accessed via SWJ-DP's JTAG mode.
design_for_test_flow_relationship_to_adi: ADIv5 SWD is layered ABOVE the SoC's classical DFT (boundary-scan, internal scan, BIST). The DAP itself is treated as part of the functional design and is itself test-scanned during production.
SoCs typically expose both ADIv5 SWD (for debug) AND IEEE 1149.1 JTAG (for boundary-scan + scan-test) via the SWJ-DP variant.

Production test sequence typically: (1) JTAG IDCODE compare, (2) JTAG boundary-scan continuity test, (3) JTAG internal scan / ATPG vectors, (4) BIST via JTAG RUNBIST, (5) switch to SWD mode and verify SWD IDCODE/DPIDR, (6) SWD-based flash programming + functional verification.
ADIv5 SWD enables in-system functional verification during production test using the same probe that programs the flash.
data_formats_supported_by_adiv5: CoreSight ROM Table — published at MEM-AP.BASE, enumerates debug components.
CoreSight Trace formats — ITM packets, DWT packets, ETM packets — defined by separate CoreSight specs.
CMSIS-DAP protocol — Arm's open USB-side protocol for debug probes; defines host-to-probe commands that the probe translates into SWD wire-level transactions.
OpenOCD / pyOCD / probe-rs — open-source host-side libraries that consume ADIv5 directly.
GDB / LLDB Remote Serial Protocol — debugger-side protocol that the host probe firmware adapts to/from SWD.
fields.notes: ADIv5 SWD is the modern Arm debug-access story documented by ARM IHI 0031C. From a classical-DFT perspective, SWD is NOT a boundary-scan architecture — it cannot drive output pins from a scan ring or observe input pins outside the CPU's own debug-control registers. To get true boundary-scan, an SoC must also implement the IEEE 1149.1 TAP, typically via the SWJ-DP's JTAG mode. ADIv6 (Arm IHI 0074) is the successor; it adds 64-bit addressing and hierarchical ROM Tables but preserves the SWD wire-level format.
